Please read the manuscript in /papers/investigations-6/03_volterra_coefficient_dynamics/01_cluster_gap_transport/02_complex_p_mellin, and some of the recent notes. I'm wondering if there might be any conserved quantities for this hierarchy. Could you look into that question? 

Note that a parallel investigation is continuing with the research there, so please put any notes in the brainstorm folder, and record chat history in a new file. If this seems promising, we can start a new investigation around this idea.

I’ll read the manuscript, recent notes, and the project’s established results, then look for conserved quantities in the hierarchy. I’ll keep this exploration in the brainstorm folder and create a separate chat-history record.

I found the requested manuscript and its own brainstorm folder. I’ll distinguish quantities conserved by the full zero dynamics from identities that need an accumulated forcing term; that distinction matters for whether they can constrain collisions.

The manuscript’s pair laws expose an important issue: low-order quantities keep exchanging information with higher moments and the exterior zeros. I’m checking whether that exchange cancels in a larger conserved quantity, and whether any such quantity remains useful when a gap closes.

There are genuine conserved quantities for finite polynomial heat flows, and this connects to known Burgers/Calogero–Moser pole dynamics. The main obstacle is transferring them to a finite block of the infinite divisor: the exterior supplies a nonzero flux. I’ve found a candidate balance law that cancels common translation and isolates the effect of variation in that exterior field. I’ll check it algebraically and against a collision example.

The checks support two distinct findings. A nontrivial quartic invariant stays positive through an exact collision, so its sign alone cannot protect a gap. For a block inside a larger divisor, I also verified the exterior flux exactly. Its translation and linear terms cancel in a useful way, leaving a possible route to sharper joint bounds—but no canonical improvement has been established yet.

Yes. I found genuine conserved quantities for finite polynomial heat flows, and a promising balance law for blocks of the full hierarchy.

For a complete degree-\(N\) heat polynomial, let \(y_i\) be its roots measured from their mean, and \(p_k=\sum_i y_i^k\). Then, for \(N\ge4\),
\[
C_4=\frac{2N-3}{4N(N-1)}p_2^2-\frac14p_4
\]
is conserved. This connects to the known integrability of finite Burgers pole dynamics. [Prior literature](https://doi.org/10.1088/1751-8113/40/20/014)

The important qualification is that **a positive conserved \(C_4\) can survive a collision**. I checked this explicitly on the manuscript’s quartic control. The invariant carries shape information, but its sign alone cannot protect a gap.

For a finite block inside the complete divisor, I derived
\[
C_4'-8R_z(c)\,C_4=\mathcal E_4,
\]
where \(R\) is the complete exterior field. Common translation cancels, and \(\mathcal E_4\) depends on the nonlinear variation of that field. An exactly affine exterior gives a conserved quantity after an integrating factor. I obtained an explicit curvature bound and a combined contour formula that preserves these cancellations; the finite checks passed in exact rational arithmetic.

I also derived a scoped obstruction to universal invariants involving only finitely many freely variable \(S/T\) moments. It leaves theta-specific constraints and infinite functionals open.

**My assessment:** the block invariant with exterior flux deserves a bounded follow-up against the current centered contour method. There is no demonstrated canonical gain yet, so I would test that comparison before starting a sustained new investigation.

Saved the [research note, derivations and checks](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/03_volterra_coefficient_dynamics/01_cluster_gap_transport/02_complex_p_mellin/brainstorm/notes/05_CONSERVED_QUANTITIES_FEASIBILITY_20261118.md) in brainstorm, with a [separate chat-history record](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/03_volterra_coefficient_dynamics/01_cluster_gap_transport/02_complex_p_mellin/brainstorm/chat-histories/README.md).

Let's start a subinvestigation, so that the current one can draw from it without it derailing the other line of thinking. Can you start the new sub-investigation following the INVESTIGATION_SETUP_WORKFLOW, but don't populate the research plan or progress file yet, just the overview and README. Can you then write a draft manuscript to derive all of the results here, and any new results from a bounded follow up? You can use any parent manuscripts as background and cite them.

I’ll set up a separate subinvestigation using the repository workflow, with an overview and README but no research plan or progress file. Then I’ll carry out a bounded follow-up and write a manuscript deriving the results, citing the parent work.

The new branch will be `01_conservation_laws` beneath the current investigation. For the bounded follow-up, I’ll test whether the exterior-field cancellation extends to all finite heat invariants and gives a quantified error reduction from shared contour data, with coordinate errors included. The manuscript will distinguish those results from any still-unproved benefit for canonical gaps.

The new branch is set up, with its research plan and progress folders left empty. The bounded follow-up has produced a useful extension: each homogeneous finite-block invariant has an exact exterior-flux law, with cancellations that reduce a specific contour error bound. I’m now deriving this carefully in the manuscript, including the costs of uncertain root locations and the collision examples that limit what conservation alone can prove.

The main distinction is now clear. A complete finite polynomial has genuine conserved coefficients; a finite block inside the full divisor exchanges those quantities with its exterior. The draft will keep both facts visible, including a positive conserved value that still permits a collision.

The error comparison is precise: with exact block coordinates, the combined contour kernel reduces the stated separate-bound allowance by a factor of at least \((\rho/A)^2\), where \(\rho\) is the block radius and \(A\) the contour radius. A symmetric quartet admits a cubic factor. I’ve also derived a coordinate-error allowance, since uncertainty in the roots can consume that gain.

The full draft is written and has compiled. It covers the original results and the bounded extension, with proofs and citations to the parent manuscripts. The exact rational checks agree across the root-velocity, exterior-flux, and contour-residue calculations. I’m finishing the mathematical scope review, page-layout check, and continuation note.

The 17-page draft is complete, and I’ve checked every rendered page. The mathematical review is recorded as a same-assistant check. The branch includes a continuation prompt but no populated research plan or progress file; the parent has only a navigation link to the new work.

Created the [conservation-laws subinvestigation](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/03_volterra_coefficient_dynamics/01_cluster_gap_transport/02_complex_p_mellin/01_conservation_laws/README.md), with its overview populated and research-plan/progress files left empty.

The **17-page draft** derives the earlier results and adds:

- A general exterior-flux law for homogeneous finite heat invariants.
- Quadratic and symmetric-quartet cubic reductions of a specified contour-error allowance.
- Explicit costs for uncertain root coordinates.

Exact rational checks passed, and every PDF page was inspected. Mathematical review remains same-assistant; no canonical gap improvement is claimed.
